It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. div.head: ECf retr 36
div.ab: De latronibus interfectis pro latrocinio. Si post iusticiam factam fecerit quis clamorem ad iusticiarium, quod iniuste interfectus sit et quod iniuste iacet inter latrones, et dixerit, quod uelit hoc dirationari, det uadimonium suum et inueniat plegios.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 666 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: Of thieves killed for theft. If, after justice has been done, anyone makes a complaint to the justiciar that [a man] was killed unjustly and that he lies unjustly among thieves, and says that he wishes to deraign (prove) this, let him give his gage and find pledges.
